HYPOTHESIS (final, data-grounded)

In the PCA of the twelve forms-of-capital indicators sampled at hundred-year slices (37 centennial points, 4100–500 BCE, standardized), the symbolic-capital components house size, daggers, and hatchets/swords are characterized as follows.

On PC1 (32.4% of variance) the three symbolic components all load with the same sign and comparable moderate magnitude on the same pole (house size −0.17, daggers −0.23, hatchets/swords −0.28), sharing it with the wealth/monumental indicators (copper+gold −0.37, depots −0.33, monument size −0.24, monument count −0.15) and standing opposite to the pottery/cultural pole (pottery form +0.41, pottery decoration −0.39). They therefore behave as a coherent, internally consistent "symbolic / prestige capital" block on PC1 rather than a scattered set.

On PC2 (16.4% of variance) they do not form a tight cluster: they spread into an ordered gradient. In the primary (raw-data) analysis, house size sits at the most negative extreme (loading −0.37), daggers are intermediate (−0.20), and hatchets/swords lie closest to zero (−0.14), i.e., the ordering house size < daggers < hatchets/swords. This graded spread lies within a broad margin of the temporal PC2 scores (the 37 centennial scores span ≈ −3.5 to +2.5, std ≈ 1.4), so house size stands apart as the most distinctive symbolic marker on PC2, while daggers and hatchets/swords occupy moderate, close positions; the relative order of the latter two is the least stable part of the pattern (their PC2 loadings swap in the interpolated-binned robustness check, within ≈ 0.05).

Declared assumptions: (1) the 12 available Z indicators are the PCA input (symbolic: HatchetSword, Dagger, HouseSize; social: CopperGold, Amber, MonumentCount; cultural: PotteryForm, PotteryDecoration; economic: Depot, Sickle, AxesCelts, MonumentSize); (2) the "hundred-year time slices" are the 37 raw centennial points (4100–500 BCE), with the interpolated 100-yr binned series used only as a robustness check (not primary); (3) PCA loading signs are convention-dependent, so conclusions rely on same-pole vs. opposite-pole relations and on relative positions, not on absolute signs.

payload.hypothesis: In the PCA of the twelve forms-of-capital indicators sampled at hundred-year slices (37 centennial points, 4100–500 BCE, standardized), the symbolic-capital components house size, daggers, and hatchets/swords load together with the same sign and comparable moderate magnitude on the same pole of PC1 (house size −0.17, daggers −0.23, hatchets/swords −0.28), sharing it with the wealth/monumental indicators and opposite the pottery pole, i.e. they act as a coherent symbolic/prestige-capital axis. On PC2 they do not cluster but spread into an ordered gradient: house size at the most negative extreme (−0.37), daggers intermediate (−0.20), hatchets/swords closest to zero (−0.14) — ordering house size < daggers < hatchets/swords — within a broad margin of temporal PC2 scores (≈ −3.5 to +2.5), making house size the most distinctive symbolic marker while daggers and hatchets/swords occupy moderate close positions.
payload.workflow: 1) Cargué time_series_data.csv y aislé los 37 puntos centenarios (CE −4100…−500) con los 12 valores Z crudos. 2) Estandaricé a varianza unitaria y apliqué PCA por eigendecomposición de la matriz de covarianza (numpy; sklearn no disponible). 3) Extraje varianza explicada, loadings PC1/PC2 y scores temporales PC1/PC2. 4) Chequeo de robustez: PCA sobre las series interpoladas (_inter) bineadas a medias de 100 años (37 bins) y comparé los 12 loadings (r=0.996 en PC1, r=0.978 en PC2) y el comportamiento de las tres simbólicas. 5) Redacté la hipótesis final en lenguaje natural con supuestos declarados.
